newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen lower, extends Monday slide.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen lower, extends Monday slide.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open lower Tuesday after falling yesterday in a retracement from last week's run-up amid moderate weather in much of the U.S. West.
"We're still seeing more testing on the downside," said an East Coast electricity broker.

In over-the-counter business, July Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $32.00-32.40 a megawatt hour (MWh) versus Monday's settlement at $32.71, and July California-Oregon Border (COB) was discussed at $20.10-20.35 against yesterday's close at $20.34.
The July power contracts will expire Wednesday.
Forecasts of mild temperatures and expectation of more generation coming back in the West will likely put more downward pressure on power futures, market sources said.
Temperatures in the Southwest were forecast to average between zero and five degrees F below normal through mid-week, rising to near normal to above normal by the end of the month.
Northwest temperatures were forecast at four to eight degrees below normal through mid-week, rising to above normal by next week.
A 750 megawatt (MW) Four Corners coal-fired unit in New Mexico and the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state are scheduled to restart tomorrow.
Analysts pegged technical suppport for July PV near $30.00 and July COB in the $18.00-20.00 range.
The power complex could stablize or test the upside if the natural gas market climbs again on rising usage from power producers to meet air-conditioning demand, traders said.
NYMEX July Henry Hub natgas, which expire Thursday, opened up 1.9 at $2.265 per million British thermal units.

Separately, the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) board is expected to approve a plan later this week, which calls for the Pacific Intertie transmission system to be derated from July 1-30 to 6,300 megawatt (MW) from the current limit of 7,200 MW.
